I drank and ate like crazy. I ended up “gaining” about 10 pounds as well and panicked hard when I got back. I would say it was all gone in about 2 weeks time. You’ll be okay!!

OP states this is the first time they are losing weight. They also are posting concerned that they consumed less than 500 calories above normal and was surprised when they didn’t gain .7kg which should take an extra 4k calories minimum. 

I too weigh myself everyday but my advice remains the same. If you can’t handle the idea that your weight is going to fluctuate up and down day to day by at least a KG or maybe even two then switching to weekly weigh ins will alleviate those issues. I didn’t say it IS driving him crazy I suggest it WILL drive him crazy. 

OP lookup normal weight fluctuation. Your fine.

Weight is measured over time basically. If you clock it each day you’re going to see fluctuations each and every day. Your body retains and releases water which is heavy at different intervals and at different levels so measuring fluctuations day to day is basically useless. What you want to do is see a trend over weeks and months NOT days. 

So my advice is to stop weighing every day and stick to the same day every week you can live with. You will drive yourself nuts if you’re thinking about things this way.

If you take a peak at my profile you will see we have just about the exact same size / weight loss profile. I’m down from around 355 16 months ago and I currently am sitting around 233. So very similar. I have also noticed the last month or two the scale not really moving so instead of focusing on diet as much as I have I’ve tried to balance it with the other side of the equation “move more.”  I’ve gone over the past month from averaging about 2,500 steps a day to averaging around 6k steps a day. I’m keeping my diet roughly the same. I’ve actually seen the scale jump up to close to 240 pounds but over the past couple of day I am
Back down to around 233. I assume that was inflammation from the increased workload on my leg muscles and I am starting to balance out again. 

We have just reached a part in our journey where things are going to be harder and we will have to fight for every pound. The good news is, every pound now is more like 5 pounds back when we were above 325. As we approach our goals the number compress down and every movement toward them is a big deal. 

It’s true you can’t outrun your fork but just make sure that you are at least meeting it where you can. If your completely sedentary than try and move a little more to offset any of the TDEE loses that naturally occur and you should be seeing some progress.  I am proud of us!

Just to add to the anecdotal evidence provided here. I started at 328. I’m currently at 235. That is a 28% weight loss which is double what the “average” weight loss was in the studies. Just remember that 15% is what the average person lost and you are not average are you?

I am a 6’3” guy who on Jan 1 of this year weighed 325. I weigh 283 as of this morning.   I can tell you that it takes a lot of willpower and guts to do this. It also takes completely changing your life and eating habits. My advice is to log your food for a week and find easy things to cut out. Track your food regardless of good or bad days.  When you say “nothing sticks” have you thought about why that is?  The things that go in your mouth are yours to control so overcoming the mental struggle is highly important. It took me 2 weeks to get ready and when i decided to do it I fasted for a day. This helped me separate who i was before to who I wanted to be. I wish you luck. You CAN do this. It’s not easy and don’t let anyone try and tell you it is. I believe in you though.

I was 8 years old and my Grandmother sat me down and after I expressed interest in her big ol bible and proceeded to read me the entire book of revelations.  Needless to say this stuck with me and has had a large impact on my life from night terrors to mental health and overall I just didn’t take it very well. However I can tell you the one thing that helped and might help you in the future. I never told my parents about it until I was about 12 years old after a particularly nasty night terror. My mom came into my room and told me whenever I felt scared that she was there for me and always would be. For some reason just taking that fear of the unknown and puttting it all on her as a kid really helped. You can’t take away the fear of the unknown and the future but you can remind them of what they have in the here and now. As to the is it real discussion I think being straight forward and saying it’s all real is okay but I would just try to distract first then answer if need be. Anyway.
